chunks: Sulayman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayyub al-Lakhmi informed me in what he wrote to me from Isfahan, saying: Abd al-Aziz and Mu'az ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi narrated to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), on the authority of Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Faith is recognition by the heart, expression by the tongue, and action by the limbs.
ai.seo_question: What are the three essential components of faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the pristine chain of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, establishes the Shia definition of faith as a comprehensive triad integrating internal conviction (ma'rifah), verbal declaration (iqrar), and physical action (amal). It underscores the inseparability of belief and practice, a key distinction in Shia theology where mere intellectual assent is insufficient without ritual and ethical observance. This formulation aligns with the broader Sunni-Shia consensus on the components of iman while emphasizing the necessity of outward manifestation of inner belief.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-4 In what Soleiman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayyoub al-Lakhmi wrote to me from Isfahan, he narrated that Ali ibn Abdul Aziz and Ma’az ibn al-Muthanna quoted on the authority of Abdul Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, on the authority of Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (s), on the authority of his father Musa ibn Ja’far (s), on the authority of his father Ja’far ibn Muhammad (s), on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali (s), on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Hussein (s), on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali (s), on the authority of his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (s) that God’s Prophet (s) said, “Faith is recognition by the heart, expression by the tongue and enacting by the body parts.”
